datasets.title: WSEFEP: FACS codes and judge ratings of 210 photographs
datasets.license: CC BY (article; codes from its supplementary Data Sheet 1)
datasets.provided: Per-photograph FACS codes with intensities (one certified coder) for 210 portrayals by 30 trained displayers (six emotions and neutral), with each photograph's judge agreement, purity and rated intensity (1,362 judges; 10 to 42 per photograph).
datasets.method: Shares of photographs with each action by displayed emotion (Wilson intervals); agreement with and without each action within each emotion (Mann-Whitney, FDR); classification of the displayed emotion from the coded actions with folds grouped by displayer and a permutation test.
caveats: Photographs were pre-selected for the facial actions the authors targeted and for the highest judge agreement, so action frequencies describe this stimulus set and agreement has a restricted range.
Portrayals elicited with an emotion-recall technique are counted as posed production here; the authors describe them as expressions of felt emotion.
One FACS coder; no reliability reported.
Copy of the supplementary appendix taken from the public repository of Stöckli et al. (2018).
In this copy the displayers’ initials are replaced with numbered codes (D01 to D30), in the same order.

datasets.title: Kunz et al., 2013, Table 1
datasets.provided: Table 1: AU frequencies by pain, pain-disgust, pure disgust (FACS (44 AUs); two FACS coders scored frequency and intensity (5-point) of all AUs with onset in the 5-s window; inter-rater reliability .90 (15% of segments))
datasets.method: Event counts per 100 observation windows as printed in the table; no intervals and no pooling, because the counts are not shares of windows.
caveats: Table 1 'Frequencies of those facial Action Units (AUs) with a critical frequency of occurrence of more than 5 % during pain and disgust stimulation, respectively.' Percent of trials (5-s video segments). States: pain = painful heat (individual pain threshold +3°C, 5-s plateau); pure disgust = authors' “pure” disgust pictures (e.g., bodily excrements); pain-disgust = disgust pictures with pain-related content (e.g., mutilation). n = 600 trials per condition = 60 participants x 10 segments per condition analysed per subject (Methods: '20 video segments for thermal stimulation (10 painful and 10 non-painful) and 30 segments of picture presentation (10 neutral, 10 pain-disgust and 10 “pure” disgust) were analyzed per subject'); no excluded segments are reported. k left empty: percentages are rounded to whole percent, so p x n is not exact. No percentages are given for the control conditions (non-painful heat, neutral pictures); only effect sizes vs control (copied into notes). Skipped combined-AU rows (published values: percent, effect size): AU1/2 brow raiser (pain 14%, d = .47; “pure” disgust 15%, d = .56; pain-disgust 15%, d = .33); AU6/7 orbit tightening (pain 52%, d = 1.08; “pure” disgust 31%, d = 1.35; pain-disgust 36%, d = 1.32); AU9/10 Levator contraction (pain 8%, d = .68; “pure” disgust 11%, d = .55; pain-disgust 14%, d = .55); AU25/26/27 mouth opening (pain 24%, d = 0.73; “pure” disgust 7%, d = .44; pain-disgust 10%, d = .49). Effect size vs control (non-painful heat) as printed: 'd = 0.96'

datasets.title: Scherer et al., 2019, Table 2A
datasets.provided: Table 2A: AU frequencies by Amusement, Anger, Boredom, Contempt, Disgust, Enjoyment, Fear, Happiness, Interest, Pride, Relief, Sadness, Surprise (FACS (manual, frame-by-frame: onset/apex/offset); each video coded by one of 11 certified FACS coders (inter-coder reliability 0.65-0.87, mean 0.75; presence/absence))
datasets.method: Proportions with Wilson 95% intervals by state; across studies, random-effects pooling on the logit scale where at least two studies report the same action, state and type of study.
caveats: Table 2A 'Percentage of actors displaying a particular AU when enacting a given emotion.' 20 professional actors (10 male, 10 female), each enacting each of 13 emotions once as a short affect burst with an /aah/ vocalization after a scenario (Stanislavski-like enactment). k = p x 20 (every published percentage is a multiple of 5, so k is exact). state 'Enjoyment' = table column header 'Enjoy'. Table 2A has no combined-AU rows (AU combinations are in Table 2C, not extracted). Table footnote (publisher page): 'Percentages >30 are bolded to provide better visibility of the major patterns.'

datasets.title: Scherer et al., 2019, Table 2B (column 'Occurrence in percent of frames')
datasets.provided: Table 2B (column 'Occurrence in percent of frames'): AU frequencies by overall (all 13 emotions) (FACS (manual, frame-by-frame: onset/apex/offset); each video coded by one of 11 certified FACS coders (inter-coder reliability 0.65-0.87, mean 0.75; presence/absence))
datasets.method: Proportions with Wilson 95% intervals by state; across studies, random-effects pooling on the logit scale where at least two studies report the same action, state and type of study.
caveats: Table 2B 'Occurrence and mean duration (s) of AU presence across actors.' is NOT a percentage-of-actors table. Table footnote (publisher page): 'Column 1—Overall percentage of video frames (of the 78,398 frames coded in total) in which the different AUs occurred'. One value per AU, not split by emotion (the text describes 260 recordings: 20 actors x 13 emotions); n = 78,398 frames from that footnote. k left empty: p is rounded to 0.1 percentage point, so p x n is not exact. The per-emotion duration columns of Table 2B are not used here.

wsefep.design: Multinomial logistic regression (scikit-learn, standardized, balanced class weights, C = 1), 5-fold cross-validation grouped by displayer, seven displayed categories.
notes: High accuracy is expected by construction: photographs were selected for the targeted facial actions and for judge agreement. It shows that the coded actions separate the selected portrayals, not that the actions reveal emotions.

datasets.design: 210 posed photographs by 30 trained displayers (six emotions and neutral), FACS-coded by one certified coder; photographs were selected for the targeted actions and high judge agreement.
datasets.caveat: Selected for the targeted actions, so reliability is inflated relative to unselected portrayals.

datasets.design: 20 professional actors each enacted 13 emotions in scenarios; FACS coding of the whole portrayal (Table 2A: share of actors showing each action).
datasets.caveat: Enacted emotions (actors), coded over whole portrayals; specificity is relative to the 13 enacted emotions only.
